sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举办的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.

sentences.en: After trying and failing to deliver Brexit,
sentences.zh: 在尝试交付脱欧协议失败后，

sentences.en: Today, the story of how the man expected to succeed her made Brexit, and how Brexit is now making him Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲述那位被寄予厚望的继任者是如何促成脱欧的，以及脱欧又是如何将他推上首相之位的。

sentences.en: It's Monday, July 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月22日，星期一。

sentences.en: I will shortly leave the job that it has been the honour of my life to hold.
sentences.zh: 我很快就要离开这个我一生引以为傲的职位了。

sentences.en: I do so with no ill will, but with enormous and enduring gratitude to have had the opportunity to serve the country I love.
sentences.zh: 我离开时没有怨恨，只有对能有机会服务于我所热爱的国家而怀有的巨大且持久的感激之情。

sentences.en: Sarah Lyle, you've covered Britain for years.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·莱尔，你报道英国新闻多年了。

sentences.zh: 嗯，这立即引发了一场关于谁来接替她的疯狂争夺。

sentences.en: And under party rules, the next party leader is chosen only by members of the Conservative Party.
sentences.zh: 根据党内规定，下一任党魁只能由保守党成员选出。

sentences.en: And it's they who will be selecting the next leader of the party, and thus the next Prime Minister of the UK.
sentences.zh: 正是他们将选出下一任党魁，进而选出下一任英国首相。

sentences.en: And who is that expected to be at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么目前来看，谁最有可能胜出？

sentences.en: At this point, it's a shoo-in for Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 目前来看，鲍里斯·约翰逊胜券在握。

sentences.en: Unless something bizarre happens, he will be the next Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 除非发生什么离奇的事情，否则他将是下一任首相。

sentences.en: My cast away this week is a politician and a journalist prone to getting into scrapes, a word that suits his rather Woodhousian image.
sentences.zh: 本周我的漂流者是一位容易惹麻烦的政客兼记者，这个词很符合他那种伍德豪斯式的形象。

sentences.en: And he was talking about his coverage.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了自己的报道。

sentences.zh: 他说，我在布鲁塞尔写的一切，我发现就像是，我只是把这些石头扔过花园的墙。

sentences.en: I listened to this amazing crash from the greenhouse next door over in England as everything I wrote from Brussels was having this amazing explosive effect on the Tory party.
sentences.zh: 我听到了隔壁英国温室里传来的惊人破碎声，因为我在布鲁塞尔写的一切对保守党产生了惊人的爆炸性影响。

sentences.en: And it really gave me this, I suppose, rather weird sense of power.

sentences.zh: 换句话说，他会为了度过难关，为了留在职位上，不惜一切代价掩盖问题。

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.zh: 他当市长时的情况是，你知道，那是他第一次拥有那么大的权力。

sentences.en: And he was fantastic figurehead.
sentences.zh: 他是一个出色的形象代言人。

sentences.en: He was a fantastic front man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个出色的门面人物。

sentences.en: Finally, you have brought home a great truth about our country.
sentences.zh: 最后，你们带回了一个关于我们国家的伟大真理。

sentences.en: That when we put our mind to it, there is absolutely nothing that this country cannot achieve.
sentences.zh: 那就是当我们下定决心时，这个国家绝对没有什么做不到的。

sentences.en: He was not a details person.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个注重细节的人。

sentences.en: He showed up late to things.
sentences.zh: 他出席活动总是迟到。

sentences.en: He was ill-prepared.
sentences.zh: 他准备不足。

sentences.en: He wouldn't read anything.
sentences.zh: 他什么都不读。

sentences.en: He didn't know about the policies.
sentences.zh: 他不了解政策。

sentences.en: And luckily, the mayor of London isn't that important a job, really.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，伦敦市长其实并不是什么重要的职位。

sentences.en: He doesn't have a lot of responsibilities, so he couldn't really mess it up.
sentences.zh: 他没有多少责任，所以他也没法把事情搞砸。

sentences.en: But he was not a great mayor.
sentences.zh: 但他并不是一位伟大的市长。

sentences.en: So Boris Johnson has been a consistent source of kind of amusement and controversy.
sentences.zh: 所以鲍里斯·约翰逊一直是一种娱乐和争议的来源。

sentences.en: Boris is constantly getting himself into trouble and constantly finding a way out of it through basically charm and bluster and an ability to talk himself out of any situation.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯总是让自己陷入麻烦，又总是能通过魅力、虚张声势以及从任何困境中脱身的能力找到出路。

sentences.en: And like what trouble does he get himself out of?
sentences.zh: 他都能摆脱什么样的麻烦？

sentences.en: Well, there's been a lot of trouble with women.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在女性问题上惹过不少麻烦。

sentences.en: He fathered a child with someone other than his wife while he was mayor of London and managed to never really have to discuss it publicly.
sentences.zh: 他在担任伦敦市长期间与妻子以外的女性生了一个孩子，并设法从未在公开场合讨论过这件事。

sentences.en: When he was editor of The Spectator, he had an affair with one of his employees who got pregnant, wrote about it.
sentences.zh: 当他担任《旁观者》杂志编辑时，他与一名员工发生了婚外情，对方怀孕了，他还写了相关文章。

sentences.en: He denied in the beginning he'd had the affair.
sentences.zh: 起初他否认有过这段婚外情。

sentences.en: He lied to the journalist who asked.
sentences.zh: 他欺骗了询问他的记者。

sentences.en: He lied to the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 他欺骗了首相。

sentences.en: He got fired from his job.
sentences.zh: 他被解雇了。

sentences.en: And somehow he got out of that too.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，他也从那件事中脱身了。

sentences.en: And it started to become clear that his disheveled, bumbling persona was calculated.
sentences.zh: 人们开始明白，他那种邋遢、笨拙的形象是刻意营造的。

sentences.en: And people have said, and I've seen it too, before he goes on TV,
sentences.zh: 人们说过，我也亲眼见过，在他上电视之前，

sentences.en: he'll run his hands through his hair to make it look messier as if he couldn't be bothered to ever brush it.
sentences.zh: 他会用手抓乱头发，让它看起来更乱，好像他从来懒得梳头一样。

sentences.en: He wants to look like that.
sentences.zh: 他想看起来就是那样。

sentences.en: And someone recently told this amazing story about how
sentences.zh: 最近有人讲了一个很棒的故事，说

sentences.en: Boris came to speak at some kind of civic meeting or meeting of some, you know, industry group and arrived five minutes late,
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯去参加某种市政会议或某个行业团体的会议，迟到了五分钟，

sentences.en: right before he was supposed to speak and sort of got up and sort of looked and said, where am I speaking?
sentences.zh: 就在他要发言之前，他站起来看了看说，我在哪里发言？

sentences.en: What group is this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么团体？

sentences.en: And told these sort of anecdotes and how he totally snowed the crowd.
sentences.zh: 然后他讲了些趣闻，把观众完全忽悠住了。

sentences.en: The crowd thought it was hilarious.
sentences.zh: 观众觉得这太搞笑了。

sentences.en: They loved him.
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢他。

sentences.en: And the guy was really happy.
sentences.zh: 那个人当时真的很开心。

sentences.en: He pulled it off until he saw Boris do the exact same thing at a totally different group some months later.
sentences.zh: 他成功了，直到几个月后他看到鲍里斯在另一个完全不同的团体那里做了同样的事情。

sentences.en: The exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 完全一样的事情。

sentences.en: He came late.
sentences.zh: 他迟到了。

sentences.en: He said, you know, where am I?
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我在哪儿？

sentences.en: He told the same anecdotes as if it was just off the top of his head.
sentences.zh: 他讲了同样的趣闻，就好像是即兴发挥一样。

sentences.en: And in fact, it was a routine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一套流程。

sentences.en: It was a routine.
sentences.zh: 这是一套流程。

sentences.en: It was a comedy routine designed to promote this view of him as this disheveled, bumbling person who could sort of pull it out at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 这是一套喜剧流程，旨在宣传他那种邋遢、笨拙，却能在最后一刻力挽狂澜的形象。

sentences.en: He wants to seem that way.
sentences.zh: 他想表现出那种样子。

sentences.en: So a lot of this is an act.
sentences.zh: 所以这很大程度上是在演戏。

sentences.en: It's kind of political theater.
sentences.zh: 这是一种政治表演。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And during that whole time, when people asked him, did he want to be prime minister?
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，当人们问他是否想当首相时，

sentences.en: What was he going to do next?
sentences.zh: 他下一步打算做什么？

sentences.en: He would always slough it off with what looked like more of an act.
sentences.zh: 他总是用一种看起来更像是在演戏的方式搪塞过去。

sentences.en: So is there a possibility you could become prime minister?
sentences.zh: 那么你有可能成为首相吗？

sentences.en: I think that that is vanishing.
sentences.zh: 我认为那微乎其微。

sentences.en: I mean, I've about as much chance of being reincarnated as an olive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我转世成一颗橄榄的几率都比那大。

sentences.en: And so meanwhile, though, he is quietly consolidating his popularity and preparing in his head somehow a way to challenge the prime minister, David Cameron.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他却在悄悄巩固自己的人气，并在脑海中构思如何挑战首相戴维·卡梅伦。

sentences.en: He's way more popular than David Cameron, though he's just an MP at this point.
sentences.zh: 他比戴维·卡梅伦受欢迎得多，尽管他当时只是一名议员。

sentences.en: And the question is, how would he get there?
sentences.zh: 问题是，他该如何达到那个位置？

sentences.en: What would he do?
sentences.zh: 他会怎么做？

sentences.en: And then finally in 2016, he sees a chance.
sentences.zh: 最后在2016年，他看到了机会。

sentences.en: And what is that chance?
sentences.zh: 那个机会是什么？

sentences.en: The chance is Brexit.
sentences.zh: 这个机会就是英国脱欧。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: Pick us up where we left off.
sentences.zh: 让我们从刚才中断的地方继续。

sentences.en: And you said that Boris Johnson sees his chance to become prime minister.
sentences.zh: 你说鲍里斯·约翰逊看到了他成为首相的机会。

sentences.en: What's happening at that moment?
sentences.zh: 那一刻发生了什么？

sentences.en: We are approaching one of the biggest decisions this country will face in our lifetimes, whether to remain in a reformed European Union or to leave.
sentences.zh: 我们正面临着我们一生中将要面对的最重大决定之一，是留在改革后的欧盟，还是离开。

sentences.en: So it was then that the prime minister, David Cameron, called the referendum known as Brexit over whether Britain would leave the European Union.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，首相戴维·卡梅伦发起了被称为“英国脱欧”的公投，决定英国是否离开欧盟。

sentences.en: The choice goes to the heart of the kind of country we want to be and the future that we want for our children.
sentences.zh: 这个选择触及了我们想要成为什么样的国家，以及我们希望为子孙后代创造什么样的未来这一核心问题。

sentences.en: He and his government were pro-Remain.
sentences.zh: 他和他的政府是支持留欧的。

sentences.en: My recommendation is clear.
sentences.zh: 我的建议很明确。

sentences.en: I believe that Britain will be safer, stronger and better off in a reformed European Union.
sentences.zh: 我相信英国在改革后的欧盟中会更安全、更强大、更富裕。

sentences.en: And everyone assumed that the country felt the same way.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以为全国人民的想法也一样。

sentences.en: And he assumes that all his allies in the Conservative Party will follow along with him.
sentences.zh: 他也以为他在保守党内的所有盟友都会跟随他。

sentences.en: Including Johnson.
sentences.zh: 包括约翰逊。

sentences.en: Including Johnson to campaign to remain.
sentences.zh: 包括约翰逊在内都要为留欧进行竞选。

sentences.en: So Johnson was one of the people who was supposed to support him.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰逊本应是支持他的人之一。

sentences.en: And at the very last minute.
sentences.zh: 但在最后一刻。

sentences.en: We have a chance actually to do something.
sentences.zh: 我们其实有机会做点什么。

sentences.en: I have a chance actually to do something.
sentences.zh: 我其实有机会做点什么。

sentences.en: Boris became head of the Leave campaign.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯成为了脱欧阵营的负责人。

sentences.en: I would like to see a new relationship based more on trade, on cooperation.
sentences.zh: 我希望看到一种更多基于贸易、合作的新关系。

sentences.en: But as I say, with much less of this supranational element.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，要减少这种超国家因素。

sentences.en: So that's where I'm coming from.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的立场。

sentences.en: Boris, if that's really what you've thought all along, why have you kept your party waiting for such a long time?
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯，如果这真的是你一直以来的想法，为什么你让你的党派等了这么久？

sentences.en: The truth is that it has been agonizingly difficult.
sentences.zh: 事实是，这极其痛苦。

sentences.en: Is it clear at this moment whether Boris Johnson actually wants to leave the EU?
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，鲍里斯·约翰逊是否真的想离开欧盟，这清楚吗？

sentences.en: Well, he wrote a famous editorial on the day he made this announcement of how he felt about it, saying we should leave the EU.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在宣布这一消息的当天写了一篇著名的社论，表达了他对此的感受，说我们应该离开欧盟。

sentences.en: Britain should leave the EU.
sentences.zh: 英国应该离开欧盟。

sentences.en: But it turned out later he'd written an opposing editorial saying the exact opposite thing.
sentences.zh: 但后来发现，他曾写过一篇相反的社论，内容截然相反。

sentences.en: It was only at the last minute that he decided to run with the we should leave version.
sentences.zh: 直到最后一刻，他才决定采用“我们应该离开”的版本。

sentences.en: Suggesting that the depth of his conviction here might have been shallow.
sentences.zh: 这表明他在这里的信念深度可能很浅。

sentences.en: Suggesting there was no depth of his conviction at all.
sentences.zh: 这表明他根本就没有什么信念深度。

sentences.en: That it was just political calculation and pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是政治算计和实用主义。

sentences.en: What would be better for Boris?
sentences.zh: 对鲍里斯来说什么更好？

sentences.en: Better for Boris how?
sentences.zh: 对鲍里斯来说怎么更好？

sentences.en: Better for Boris in that he wanted power.
sentences.zh: 对鲍里斯来说更好，因为他想要权力。

sentences.en: And what he thought would happen, what everyone thought would happen, was the following.
sentences.zh: 他认为会发生什么，每个人都认为会发生什么，就是接下来这些。

sentences.en: That Brexit would be voted down.
sentences.zh: 脱欧公投会被否决。

sentences.en: That they'd remain in the European Union.
sentences.zh: 他们会留在欧盟。

sentences.en: But that David Cameron would be so weakened by the whole process that he would have to step down as prime minister, leaving Boris in place to take over.
sentences.zh: 但戴维·卡梅伦会因为整个过程而变得非常虚弱，以至于他不得不辞去首相职务，让鲍里斯接手。

sentences.en: And then Boris would lead the country, not through Brexit, because Brexit would have been voted down.
sentences.zh: 然后鲍里斯将领导这个国家，不是通过脱欧，因为脱欧会被否决。

sentences.en: But he would have appeased the right wing of the party and thus consolidated his power better than Cameron ever could.
sentences.zh: 但他会安抚党内的右翼，从而比卡梅伦更好地巩固自己的权力。

sentences.en: So this whole kind of move to backstab David Cameron by supporting Brexit at the last minute is based on his belief that Brexit would not actually happen.
sentences.zh: 所以这种在最后一刻支持脱欧来背刺戴维·卡梅伦的举动，是基于他认为脱欧实际上不会发生。

sentences.en: Until it did.
sentences.zh: 直到它真的发生了。

sentences.en: There we are.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That is now statistically, mathematically there, that the Leave campaign have won.
sentences.zh: 现在从统计学和数学上来说，脱欧阵营已经赢了。

sentences.en: And we're expecting at the end of the count, 52% for Leave, 48% for Remain.
sentences.zh: 我们预计计票结束时，脱欧派占52%，留欧派占48%。

sentences.en: Quite an extraordinary moment.
sentences.zh: 非常非凡的时刻。

sentences.en: Everybody was shocked.
sentences.zh: 每个人都震惊了。

sentences.en: And if you see, there was an amazing moment where Boris Johnson comes out.
sentences.zh: 如果你看的话，有一个惊人的时刻，鲍里斯·约翰逊出来了。

sentences.en: Today, I think all of us politicians...
sentences.zh: 今天，我想我们所有的政客……

sentences.en: The head of this campaign...
sentences.zh: 这场竞选的负责人……

sentences.en: ...should thank the British people...
sentences.zh: ……都应该感谢英国人民……

sentences.en: ...to give a press conference...
sentences.zh: ……去召开新闻发布会……

sentences.en: Because in a way, they have been doing our job for us.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，他们一直在替我们做我们的工作。

sentences.en: To basically reassure the country that he's in control, that he knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 基本上是为了向全国保证他在掌控局面，他知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: They hire us to deal with the hard questions.
sentences.zh: 他们雇我们来处理棘手的问题。

sentences.en: And this year, we gave them one of the biggest and toughest questions of all.
sentences.zh: 而今年，我们给了他们一个最大、最艰难的问题。

sentences.en: And he looks so frightened.
sentences.zh: 他看起来非常害怕。

sentences.en: I believe the British people have spoken up for democracy.
sentences.zh: 我相信英国人民已经为民主发声了。

sentences.en: He looks like a deer caught in the headlights.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像一只被车灯惊吓的鹿。

sentences.en: He has no plan.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何计划。

sentences.en: It becomes clear he has no plan.
sentences.zh: 很明显他没有任何计划。

sentences.en: Thank you, finally, to everybody at Vote Leave for the extraordinary and positive campaign you have run.
sentences.zh: 最后，感谢“投票脱欧”的所有人，感谢你们开展了这场非凡而积极的竞选。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Then what happens?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: It has been the greatest honor of my life to serve our country as prime minister over these last six years.
sentences.zh: 在过去六年里担任首相为我们的国家服务，是我一生中最大的荣幸。

sentences.en: So then David Cameron quits, and they're left with a power vacuum.
sentences.zh: 所以戴维·卡梅伦辞职了，留下了一个权力真空。

sentences.en: Who is going to be the next prime minister?
sentences.zh: 谁将成为下一任首相？

sentences.en: And at that point, it looked like Boris was a she-win.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，看起来鲍里斯是稳赢的。

sentences.en: He was definitely going to get it.
sentences.zh: 他肯定会得到这个职位。

sentences.en: He had been the head of the Leave campaign.
sentences.zh: 他曾是脱欧竞选的负责人。

sentences.en: He was the most popular politician in the country.
sentences.zh: 他是全国最受欢迎的政客。

sentences.en: And this is what he's always wanted.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他一直想要的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Everybody knew who he was.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道他是谁。

sentences.en: It's what he's always wanted.
sentences.zh: 这正是他一直想要的。

sentences.en: And he had a colleague, Michael Gove, who'd also betrayed Cameron and helped him help Boris with the anti-Europe campaign.
sentences.zh: 他有一位同事叫迈克尔·戈夫，他也背叛了卡梅伦，并帮助鲍里斯开展了反欧运动。

sentences.en: And the idea was that Boris would be prime minister and Michael Gove would be like chancellor of the Exchequer or some other really good job.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，鲍里斯当首相，迈克尔·戈夫担任财政大臣或其他非常重要的职位。

sentences.en: And they sort of planned it all out.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上把一切都计划好了。

sentences.en: And there really weren't any other legitimate candidates at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时确实没有其他合法的候选人了。

sentences.en: So that was like on a Friday, I think.
sentences.zh: 那大概是在一个周五，我想。

sentences.en: And there was, I think, six days to figure this out or about a week to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 我想当时有六天时间来解决这个问题，或者说大约一周的时间。

sentences.en: And they're campaigning.
sentences.zh: 他们正在竞选。

sentences.en: And everyone's like, what are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 每个人都在问，他们打算怎么做？

sentences.en: They have to put out some sort of plan.
sentences.zh: 他们必须拿出一个计划来。

sentences.en: Boris writes this editorial for The Telegraph that's supposedly putting out his political plan.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯为《每日电讯报》写了这篇社论，据说是为了阐述他的政治计划。

sentences.en: There isn't really a plan.
sentences.zh: 其实根本没有什么计划。

sentences.en: It's all chaotic.
sentences.zh: 一切都很混乱。

sentences.en: It's all weird.
sentences.zh: 一切都很古怪。

sentences.en: Everyone's getting scared.
sentences.zh: 每个人都开始感到害怕。

sentences.en: And then the day before, Boris is meant to formally announce that he is putting his name forward to be prime minister.
sentences.zh: 就在前一天，鲍里斯本应正式宣布他将提名自己竞选首相。

sentences.en: I thought it was right that following the decision that the British people took last week.
sentences.zh: 我认为，继英国人民上周做出决定之后，这样做是正确的。

sentences.en: Michael Gove, his great friend and ally through the whole campaign.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·戈夫，他在整个竞选期间的挚友和盟友。

sentences.en: And I hoped that Boris Johnson would be someone who could ensure that the government followed the instructions of the British people
sentences.zh: 我曾希望鲍里斯·约翰逊能成为一个确保政府遵循英国人民意愿的人，

sentences.en: and also build and unite a team around him in order to lead this country forward.
sentences.zh: 同时也能建立并团结一个团队，带领这个国家前进。

sentences.en: Calls a press conference and says.
sentences.zh: 他召开了新闻发布会并说道。

sentences.en: And Boris is an amazing and an impressive person.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯是一个了不起且令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: But I've realized in the last few days that Boris isn't capable of building that team and providing that unity.
sentences.zh: 但我过去几天意识到，鲍里斯没有能力建立那个团队并提供那种团结。

sentences.en: He doesn't trust Boris.
sentences.zh: 他不信任鲍里斯。

sentences.en: He thinks Boris would be a bad prime minister.
sentences.zh: 他认为鲍里斯会是个糟糕的首相。

sentences.en: Good Lord.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And he's withdrawing his support.
sentences.zh: 他正在撤回对他的支持。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: Well, I must tell you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我必须告诉你。

sentences.en: Everybody who thought Boris is going to be a prime minister is now saying he's not going to be.
sentences.zh: 所有认为鲍里斯会成为首相的人现在都说他当不成了。

sentences.en: And Boris has to withdraw from the race.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯不得不退出竞选。

sentences.en: I have concluded that person cannot be me.
sentences.zh: 我得出的结论是，那个人不应该是我。

sentences.en: This is pretty humiliating.
sentences.zh: 这真是太丢人了。

sentences.en: Really humiliating.
sentences.zh: 真的很丢人。

sentences.en: And it felt like everything had finally caught up to him.
sentences.zh: 感觉他终于遭到了报应。

sentences.en: He'd been exposed.
sentences.zh: 他被揭穿了。

sentences.en: The lying, the blundering, the sort of, you know, lack of preparation,
sentences.zh: 谎言、失误、那种，你知道的，缺乏准备，

sentences.en: the inability to follow through on things had all finally, finally come back to haunt him.
sentences.zh: 无法贯彻到底的能力，最终还是反过来困扰着他。

sentences.en: He'd always gotten away with everything before.
sentences.zh: 他以前总是能逃脱惩罚。

sentences.en: He was like the Teflon politician.
sentences.zh: 他就像个“特氟龙”政客（指丑闻不沾身）。

sentences.en: And suddenly he was having to accept the repercussions of what he had done.
sentences.zh: 而突然间，他不得不接受自己所作所为带来的后果。

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: They have to find a compromise candidate.
sentences.zh: 他们必须找到一个妥协的候选人。

sentences.en: And everyone is sort of poisoned in one way or another.
sentences.zh: 每个人在某种程度上都已经名声受损了。

sentences.en: So they settle on this super unlikely figure, Theresa May.
sentences.zh: 所以他们选定了这个极其不可能的人选，特蕾莎·梅。

sentences.en: I have just been to Buckingham Palace, where Her Majesty the Queen has asked me to form a new government.
sentences.zh: 我刚从白金汉宫回来，女王陛下已要求我组建新政府。

sentences.en: And I accept it.
sentences.zh: 我接受了。

sentences.en: And she tries and she tries.
sentences.zh: 她尝试了一次又一次。

sentences.en: And no one likes what she does.
sentences.zh: 但没人喜欢她的做法。

sentences.en: And where is Boris during all this period?
sentences.zh: 那么在这期间鲍里斯在哪里呢？

sentences.en: Well, Boris is a dangerous figure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，鲍里斯是个危险人物。

sentences.en: So she felt, the way Cameron did before, that she could sort of neuter him by giving him a job in her cabinet.
sentences.zh: 所以她觉得，就像卡梅伦之前做的那样，可以通过给她内阁的一个职位来削弱他。

sentences.en: So she makes him foreign secretary.
sentences.zh: 于是她任命他为外交大臣。

sentences.en: Another job he's not very good at.
sentences.zh: 这也是一份他不怎么擅长的工作。

sentences.en: Either they're dissembling or lying or you are.
sentences.zh: 要么是他们在掩饰或撒谎，要么是你。

sentences.en: Four ambassadors said they heard it several times.
sentences.zh: 四位大使说他们听到了好几次。

sentences.en: You said it's not government policy, but you do support free movement.
sentences.zh: 你说这不是政府政策，但你确实支持自由流动。

sentences.en: That's four of them.
sentences.zh: 那是四个人说的。

sentences.en: They're not lying.
sentences.zh: 他们没有撒谎。

sentences.en: That's complete nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这完全是胡说八道。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I think that they have been misrepresented.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他们被误解了。

sentences.en: And if I may say so, I'm not entirely convinced that your reporter talked to those ambassadors.
sentences.zh: 如果我可以这么说的话，我并不完全相信你的记者真的采访过那些大使。

sentences.en: And I think...
sentences.zh: 而且我认为……

sentences.en: He's underprepared.
sentences.zh: 他准备不足。

sentences.en: He's disheveled.
sentences.zh: 他衣冠不整。

sentences.en: He says things that aren't true.
sentences.zh: 他说的有些话不是事实。

sentences.en: And he makes some bad blunders.
sentences.zh: 他还犯了一些严重的错误。

sentences.en: But he sort of soldiers on.
sentences.zh: 但他还是硬着头皮干下去了。

sentences.en: Sounds like Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 听起来很像鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Sounds like Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 听起来很像鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: He's Boris being Boris.
sentences.zh: 这就是鲍里斯的作风。

sentences.en: And then he ends up resigning from the cabinet over what he says is Theresa May's poor handling of the Brexit negotiations.
sentences.zh: 后来他因为特蕾莎·梅对脱欧谈判处理不当而辞去了内阁职务。

sentences.en: We never actually turned that vision into a negotiating position in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上从未将那个愿景转化为布鲁塞尔的谈判立场。

sentences.en: And we never made it into a negotiating offer.
sentences.zh: 我们也从未将其转化为谈判方案。

sentences.en: Instead, we dithered.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们犹豫不决。

sentences.en: But really what he's doing is starting to plot his next move.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他所做的是开始策划他的下一步行动。

sentences.en: So the no's have it.
sentences.zh: 反对票占多数。

sentences.en: The no's have it.
sentences.zh: 反对票占多数。

sentences.en: Unlock!
sentences.zh: 解锁！

sentences.en: On a point of...
sentences.zh: 关于……的一点。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Point of order.
sentences.zh: 程序问题。

sentences.en: The Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 首相。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mr Speaker.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，议长先生。

sentences.en: Mr Speaker, the House has spoken and the government will listen.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，议会已经表态，政府会倾听。

sentences.en: It is clear that the House does not support this deal.
sentences.zh: 很明显，议会不支持这项协议。

sentences.en: But tonight's vote tells us nothing about what it does support.
sentences.zh: 但今晚的投票并没有告诉我们它支持什么。

sentences.en: Theresa May is like one of those...
sentences.zh: 特蕾莎·梅就像那些……

sentences.en: She's like, I'm afraid, like a bull in a bullring who has tons of stuff sticking out of her.
sentences.zh: 恐怕她就像斗牛场里的一头公牛，身上插满了东西。

sentences.en: You know, and she's staggering around.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她摇摇晃晃地走着。

sentences.en: And people are throwing spears at her and they're sticking it and she's bleeding and everyone's criticizing her.
sentences.zh: 人们向她投掷长矛，长矛扎在她身上，她在流血，每个人都在批评她。

sentences.en: This is so graphic.
sentences.zh: 这画面感太强了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: And she keeps coming back.
sentences.zh: 但她还是不断地回来。

sentences.en: So the no's have it.
sentences.zh: 所以反对票占多数。

sentences.en: The no's have it.
sentences.zh: 反对票占多数。

sentences.en: Unlock!
sentences.zh: 解锁！

sentences.en: And trying again and nobody likes anything she does.
sentences.zh: 再试一次，没人喜欢她做的任何事。

sentences.en: On a point of order, Mr Speaker, I profoundly regret the decision that this House has taken tonight.
sentences.zh: 程序问题，议长先生，我深感遗憾的是，本议会今晚做出了这个决定。

sentences.en: And she becomes more and more unpopular.
sentences.zh: 她变得越来越不受欢迎。

sentences.en: So the no's have it.
sentences.zh: 所以反对票占多数。

sentences.en: The no's have it.
sentences.zh: 反对票占多数。

sentences.en: Unlock!
sentences.zh: 解锁！

sentences.en: And by the end, people are almost like, whoever gets in, we prefer to Theresa May.
sentences.zh: 到最后，人们几乎觉得，不管谁上来，我们都比特蕾莎·梅强。

sentences.en: Mr Speaker, I think it should be a matter of profound regret to every member of this House that once again, we have been unable to support leaving the European Union.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，我认为本议会的每一位成员都应该深感遗憾，因为我们再次未能支持脱离欧盟。

sentences.en: So the moment that Theresa May announces that she's stepping down, Boris Johnson sees his second chance.
sentences.zh: 所以，在特蕾莎·梅宣布辞职的那一刻，鲍里斯·约翰逊看到了他的第二次机会。

sentences.en: To be prime minister.
sentences.zh: 成为首相的机会。

sentences.en: To be prime minister.
sentences.zh: 成为首相的机会。

sentences.en: Get her out and then he can go in.
sentences.zh: 把她赶走，然后他就能进去了。

sentences.en: I am pleased today.
sentences.zh: 我今天很高兴。

sentences.en: I am proud today.
sentences.zh: 我今天很自豪。

sentences.en: To introduce the candidate whom I shall support.
sentences.zh: 介绍我将要支持的候选人。

sentences.en: To lead the conservative party and our nation.
sentences.zh: 来领导保守党和我们的国家。

sentences.en: A man who has already shown that he can lead this great global city through two successful terMs.
sentences.zh: 一个已经证明他能带领这个伟大的全球城市度过两个成功任期的人。

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们，鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Sarah, are we to understand that all of this played out exactly the way that Boris Johnson would have hoped?
sentences.zh: 莎拉，我们是否可以理解为，这一切的发展完全如鲍里斯·约翰逊所愿？

sentences.en: That after he elevated Brexit, no matter what you think of it, Brexit has come around to elevate him.
sentences.zh: 在他推动脱欧之后，无论你怎么看，脱欧反过来成就了他。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想是这样的。

sentences.en: I think in the last three years since the vote, he's had to get his head around the fact this is what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我认为在投票后的过去三年里，他不得不接受这样一个事实：这就是将要发生的事情。

sentences.en: And if he has a conviction, this is now his conviction.
sentences.zh: 如果他有某种信念，这就是他现在的信念。

sentences.en: And it's a poison chalice, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一个烫手山芋。

sentences.en: I feel like he's set himself up for a task that's almost impossible to carry out.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他给自己设定了一个几乎不可能完成的任务。

sentences.en: And it's kind of ironic that he's gotten this job through something that he put into place and made it so difficult for himself.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，他通过自己一手促成的事情得到了这份工作，却也让自己陷入了如此艰难的境地。

sentences.en: His political hero is Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 他的政治偶像温斯顿·丘吉尔。

sentences.en: And he always wanted to be Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 他一直想成为温斯顿·丘吉尔。

sentences.en: And I don't see how anyone can be Winston Churchill throughout the Brexit process.
sentences.zh: 我不明白在整个脱欧过程中，有谁能成为温斯顿·丘吉尔。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: It's not like defeating the Nazis during the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 这不像二战期间击败纳粹。

sentences.en: It's not a war.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场战争。

sentences.en: It's a very, very complicated divorce from an entity that Britain is incredibly connected to in ways that most people don't understand and take for granted.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常复杂的离婚过程，涉及到一个与英国有着千丝万缕联系的实体，这种联系方式大多数人并不了解，也视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And I don't see anyone coming out of it better off than they were before.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有谁能从中获得比以前更好的结果。

sentences.en: So now this man with what appears to be no deeply rooted political views is going to be steering the U.K.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，这个看起来没有根深蒂固政治观点的人，将引导英国。

sentences.en: through its greatest political challenge.
sentences.zh: 度过它最大的政治挑战。

sentences.en: Perhaps, perhaps, in history.
sentences.zh: 也许，也许是历史上最大的挑战。

sentences.en: And it's exactly what he wanted.
sentences.zh: 这正是他想要的。

sentences.en: I'm not sure he wanted to have to be prime minister at this moment in history, but it's the only chance he's going to get.
sentences.zh: 我不确定他是否想在历史的这个时刻当首相，但这将是他唯一的机会。

sentences.en: And he has a sort of blind optimism that he will be able to figure something out when he gets a job.
sentences.zh: 他有一种盲目的乐观，认为当他得到这份工作时，他总能想出办法来。

sentences.en: And I think that's the approach he's taking now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是他现在采取的方法。

sentences.en: Sarah, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 莎拉，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And good luck in London.
sentences.zh: 祝你在伦敦好运。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm flying there soon.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很快就要飞过去了。

sentences.en: So you're going to be there for the...
sentences.zh: 所以你要去那里参加……

sentences.en: I'll be there again, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我会再去那里的，是的。

sentences.en: And I'll do what I thought I was supposed to do two years ago, the last time this came around, three years ago.
sentences.zh: 我会做我两年前，也就是三年前这件事发生时，本该做的事情。

sentences.en: Which is?
sentences.zh: 是什么？

sentences.en: I will write the story saying that Boris Johnson has become prime minister.
sentences.zh: 我会写一篇报道，说鲍里斯·约翰逊已经成为首相了。

sentences.en: That was supposed to happen before, and maybe it'll happen this time.
sentences.zh: 这本该早点发生的，也许这次会实现。

sentences.en: The winner of the conservative party election for prime minister is expected to be announced tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 保守党党魁选举的获胜者预计将于明天公布，他将出任首相。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: According to the records, the Walgreens employee in charge of flagging such orders cleared them anyway.
sentences.zh: 根据记录，负责标记此类订单的沃尔格林员工还是批准了这些订单。

sentences.en: The records show that companies had little or no oversight in place for flagging suspiciously large orders.
sentences.zh: 记录显示，各公司对于标记可疑的大额订单几乎没有或根本没有监管措施。

sentences.en: One major drug maker gave the job of stopping suspicious orders to sales staff whose bonuses were tied to those sales.
sentences.zh: 一家大型制药商将拦截可疑订单的工作交给了销售人员，而他们的奖金与这些销售额直接挂钩。

sentences.en: The records are now evidence in a major trial against the companies, brought by nearly 2,000 towns and cities, devastated by the opioid crisis.
sentences.zh: 这些记录现在已成为针对这些公司的一场重大审判中的证据，该诉讼由近2000个深受阿片类药物危机摧残的城镇联合发起。

sentences.en: So, that's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro, listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 欢迎在各大播客平台收听《地铁》。
